newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen stuck in narrow range in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen stuck in narrow range in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to trade in a narrow range against both the yen and the mark in Asia on Wednesday ahead of the release of U.S. trade data for June later Wednesday and a Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday.
The greenback is seen capped by Japanese exporter offers above 118.50 yen, but its downside is expected to limited by bids below 118 yen, traders said.
But a further slide in Tokyo stocks could weigh on the Japanese currency, traders said.
"Another construction company collapsed yesterday. People will be carefully watching stocks," said a city bank trader.

Medium-sized general contractor Daito Kogyo Co Ltd said on Tuesday it had applied for court protection from creditors with debts totalling 159.2 billion yen, becoming the third listed Japanese construction firm in less than two months to collapse.
Traders said the market is reluctant to move the dollar too far in either direction ahead of the U.S. trade data release.
Economists forecast the U.S. trade deficit will edge up slightly to $10.36 billion in June from $10.23 billion in May.
"A deficit of around $10 billion is likely to have limited impact on the market," said a trader at a trust bank.

Traders said the dollar is likely to remain well-bid against the mark as speculation of higher German interest rates waned after Buba council member Hans-Juergen Krupp said on Monday that a rate rise would be very damaging to the economy.
But operators are cautious about selling marks too aggresively before Thursday's Buba council meeting, the trust bank trader said.
"We also have the Ifo index to watch today. So people are a bit cautious about selling marks," he said.
The Ifo economic research institute will release the German business climate index for July at 0800 GMT.
The dollar ended higher against the German currency in New York on Tuesday following the Bundesbank's decision to stick with its fixed rate repo at 3.0 percent.
A nearly 115-point rise in the Dow Jones Industrial Average also helped to reassure dollar bulls.
The greenback ended at 118.25/35 yen and 1.8400/10 marks on Tuesday in New York.
